America can build the best frontier models and still lose the global AI race. Which is why Jensen’s return matters far beyond Nvidia. Governments around the world want sovereign AI: models they can run on their own soil, on their own infrastructure, under their own control. If American companies won’t meet that demand, Chinese companies will. Countries will start with Chinese models, then adopt Chinese infrastructure and chips. Having the smartest model won’t mean much if most of the world runs on someone else’s stack. We’ve seen a version of this play out with Huawei. China understood that supplying the world’s telecom infrastructure creates lasting strategic influence. Once a country builds its networks around your equipment, it also builds technical expertise, supplier relationships, and future investment around it. Replacing that equipment becomes expensive and disruptive (the US government is now trying to finance replacement operations but it’s been difficult). That’s why Jensen’s backing of the American open-model ecosystem is so important. Open models give startups the freedom to compete and give countries a reason to build on American technology. We need both frontier leadership and global adoption. Open models are essential to getting both. https://t.co/f34FKKbljl
